_comment: What kind of thing an axis measures. An EXTERNAL axis has a universe that exists whether or not the feature does: AWS Regions, resource types, operating systems. Measuring a feature against it is coverage, and the ratio means something. A CATALOGUE axis is a list the service publishes about itself: GuardDuty's finding types, Config's managed rules, Security Hub's controls. A feature always holds 100% of its own catalogue, so the ratio is an inventory count, not coverage. A catalogue axis still carries real coverage when a statement is scoped to an external axis, as with a Config rule available only in certain Regions.

managedRuleGroup.label: managed rule groups the service publishes

resourceTarget.label: resources a rule group can be attached to

conditionKey.label: IAM condition keys the service publishes

iamCapability.label: IAM capabilities a service can support

integrationType.label: how a service integrates with Organizations

sharingScope.label: how far a resource can be shared

country.label: countries and regions a data identifier is designed for

selectorField.label: advanced event selector fields the service publishes

wordpressComponentType.label: WordPress component types the scanner reads

managedRuleGroupRule.label: rules inside a managed rule group

sensitiveDataType.label: categories of sensitive data the service detects

note: kind: external means the axis is a universe that exists whether or not the service mentions it; catalogue means a list the service publishes about itself, which is counted rather than measured. universe names a closed universe file: the denominator is then every member of it, and a member the page never mentions is unknown, never not-covered. Without it the denominator is only what the page named, so a page listing 5 Regions would read 5 of 5.
